stories.title: The Secret Bat Bomb
stories.description: The bizarre WWII project that attempted to use bats armed with tiny napalm bombs to destroy cities.

scenes.visual_prompt: Extreme close-up of a screeching fruit bat. Suddenly, the camera pulls back to reveal a tiny, high-tech timed napalm canister strapped to its chest with a miniature leather harness. The bat's wings flap violently in slow motion. Audio: A piercing, high-frequency bat screech and the mechanical 'click-click-click' of a timer. High-fidelity, 4K HDR.
scenes.narration: Why would the U.S. military spend millions of dollars to turn thousands of bats into living bombs?

scenes.visual_prompt: A cinematic wide shot of a 'bomb' casing opening mid-air, releasing a cloud of thousands of bats over a model Japanese village. The sun is blocked out by the swarm. Below, tiny fires begin to ignite on thatched roofs. Audio: The deafening collective sound of thousands of flapping wings and sudden, distant 'whoosh' sounds of fire igniting.
scenes.narration: Project X-Ray was real. The plan was for these bats to roost in wooden buildings and ignite simultaneously, creating an unstoppable firestorm.

scenes.visual_prompt: A grainy, black-and-white 'top secret' document being stamped with a red 'CANCELLED' mark. In the background, a massive mushroom cloud rises slowly. Audio: A heavy, echoing rubber stamp 'thud' followed by a haunting cinematic drone. The final frame is the bat staring into the lens.
scenes.narration: It was actually more effective than the Atomic Bomb in tests. So why would they cancel it? Because the nukes were ready first. Follow for more insane science.
